activities.directions: Print your page. Write how to plant a seed. Use first, next, then and last.

writeFor: I wrote the steps in order.

successCriteria: I wrote the steps in order.
I used order words.

models.A: First, dig a hole. Next, put in the seed. Then, water it. Last, put it in the sun.
models.B: First, dig a small hole in the dirt. Next, drop the seed in the hole. Then, cover it and water it. Last, put the pot in the sun.
models.C: First, dig a small hole in the soil. Next, drop the seed in and cover it. Then, give it a little water every day. Last, put it in the sun so it can grow.

modelNotes.A: Uses all four order words with one short step each.
modelNotes.B: Uses exact action words (drop, cover) and says where.
modelNotes.C: Tells how often (every day) and uses 'so' to tell why a step matters.

modelNotes.B: Uses 'and' to join ideas and shows the feeling at the end.

activities.prompt: How are ice, water and steam different?
activities.promptEs: ¿En qué se diferencian el hielo, el agua y el vapor?
writeFor: I wrote about ice, water and steam.
I used the words solid, liquid or gas.
I used a linking word.
activities.responsePlaceholder: Ice is a ___. When it melts, it is a ___. With more heat, it becomes ___.
successCriteria: I wrote about ice, water and steam.

models.A: Ice is a solid. When it melts, it is a liquid. With more heat, it becomes a gas.
models.B: Ice is a solid. When it melts, it is a liquid called water. With more heat, it becomes a gas called steam.
models.C: Ice is a solid that keeps its shape. When ice melts, it becomes liquid water that can flow. With more heat, water becomes steam, a gas that floats into the air.

modelNotes.A: Names the state of matter for ice, water and steam in order.
modelNotes.B: Uses 'called' to connect each state to its name (water, steam).
modelNotes.C: Tells how each state acts (keeps its shape, can flow, floats) to show the difference.
